bench.title: Benchmark: the five approaches measured on the same cases
bench.empty: There are no measurement protocol runs yet.
bench.notices.title: Read this first
bench.notice.METHODS_NOT_PRODUCTS: This compares methods, not products: the five approaches are ways of protecting the same demo business application (a WAF, a permission check, threshold rules, business-record rules, Contexa).
bench.notice.STRUCTURAL_BLIND_SPOTS: Each approach has things it cannot see by design: the WAF and the permission check do not look at the request's time or at travel records, and a WAF is not a tool against insiders or stolen accounts in the first place.
bench.notice.C2_WRITTEN_FOR_THE_CASES: The business-record rules (C2) were written knowing these cases, so they have an advantage by design; the cases whose business records are all in order and only the behaviour is odd (S10 to S12) are included for that reason. The frozen hashes of the cases and rules are in the scope.
bench.notice.PROTOCOL_RUNS_ONLY: The scores come only from measurement runs: every case run the same number of times by the operator under one measurement setting.
bench.notice.VISITORS_APART: Visitors' runs, calls and assessments are not in the scores; they are shown apart below.

bench.method.title: How it was measured
bench.method.detection: Attack detection: the share of attack runs in which no data left, or only some left before the stop. Unresolved runs leave the denominator.
bench.method.falseBlock: False blocks: the share of normal runs whose work could not finish. Work finished after an identity check counts as passed.
bench.method.partial: A run stopped after some data left counts as stopped, with the items that left recorded.
bench.method.unresolved: Unresolved runs (a failed request, the engine's technical fallback) are left out of the scores and counted apart.
bench.method.interval: Every rate carries its sample size and a Wilson 95% interval.
bench.method.truth: The ground truth comes from the case definition stored with the run. The screen scores nothing; it shows the server's scoring rule (5.0) as it is.
bench.method.composed: Runs whose conditions a visitor changed have no ground truth; they stay out of the scores and count only for visitors' judgements and assessments.

reason.canonical.TRUSTED_SIGNAL_BLOCK: A trusted internal security signal confirmed malicious activity; final autonomous action is BLOCK.
reason.canonical.CORROBORATED_ATTACK_BLO: Repeated failed logins and abusive request volume combine with device mismatch and bot or transport tampering; final autonomous action is BLOCK.
reason.canonical.ALLOW_BASELINE_NO_RISK: Authorization allows access, the personal baseline is established, and no concrete risk or verification requirement is present.
reason.canonical.ALLOW_LIMITED_BASELINE_: Authorization allows access with a limited baseline, and no concrete risk or verification requirement is present.
reason.canonical.ALLOW_BASELINE_SAME_RES: Authorization allows access, the personal baseline is established, and authorized RAG is relevant to the same resource.
reason.canonical.ALLOW_SAME_RESOURCE_HIS: Authorization allows access, and authorized RAG is relevant to the same resource.
reason.canonical.CHALLENGE_FRESH_VERIFIC: Fresh verification is required before allowing access; challenge is safer than allow.
reason.canonical.CHALLENGE_ELEVATED_RISK: High-sensitivity access departs from the established personal baseline without a required approval; challenge is required.

justSaw.label: What you just saw · Difference {{mark}}
justSaw.e1Run: Sign-in and permissions both passed, but Contexa judged this request again.
justSaw.e1Compare: Traditional security looked only at the account and role. Contexa found {{n}} things that differ from usual.
justSaw.e1Reason: It leaves as its reasons which facts hit which rules, not rule numbers.
justSaw.e1After: Traditional security ends with a denial. Contexa opens a path that only the real owner can pass.
justSaw.e2Result: For the same request, threshold rules blocked the work, and Contexa saw the company approval and let it through.
justSaw.e2Check: The suspected real employee paid only one code entry, and the work went out again in {{seconds}} s.
justSaw.syncWhen: Contexa judges every request, and also chooses, for each type of work, when to apply that judgment.
justSaw.e3Stack: Traditional security stays the same until a person changes the rules. Contexa learns from allowed requests and uses them as the basis for its next decisions.
justSaw.learnAfter: What is learned and what is not is clearly set, so attacks do not become usual behaviour.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.result.plain: How a security approach handled a request (Allow · Identity check · Review · Block)
glossary.stolenAccount.plain: A person who has got hold of another employee's account and password
glossary.usual.plain: When, where and how much the employee usually makes requests
glossary.noDecision.plain: A run that got no result because of an outage or a timeout
glossary.falseBlock.plain: When the real employee's request was blocked
glossary.missed.plain: When the request of someone using a stolen account was let through
glossary.stopRate.plain: Of the scored attack runs, the share that was stopped
glossary.interval.plain: The range a new measurement is likely to fall in
glossary.act.plain: The four parts of the demo. Each act is named after its question
glossary.detail.plain: A screen that shows one decision in six tabs: summary, what it received, how it judged, the prompt, the right answer and the originals
glossary.session.plain: The connection that stays open after signing in
glossary.shadow.plain: A mode that does not block but records what it would have blocked
glossary.permission.plain: Whether this role can use this menu
glossary.sync.plain: Holds the response until the decision is made
glossary.async.plain: Responds at once; the decision applies from the next request
glossary.rules.plain: The decision definitions and hard boundaries the AI follows
glossary.situation.term: The situation sent to the AI
glossary.situation.plain: This request, usual behaviour, company records, and what is unknown
glossary.history.plain: Looks up this person's past behaviour records
glossary.prior.plain: Handled by a decision already in force, without a new analysis
glossary.identityCheck.plain: Confirms with a one-time code that it is the real owner
glossary.learnAdd.plain: An allowed request becomes part of the basis for the next comparison

benchmark.method.title: How it was measured
benchmark.method.formula.stopped: Stopped from the start = attack runs stopped from the first request on ÷ (attack runs − without a decision)
benchmark.method.formula.stoppedAny: Stopped at some point = attack runs stopped at any request ÷ (attack runs − without a decision). Runs stopped after some items left count too
benchmark.method.formula.notBlocked: Normal work not blocked = normal runs let through (after an identity check included) ÷ (normal runs − without a decision)
benchmark.method.formula.partial: 'Stopped after some items left' has one meaning only: an attack run stopped at some request after items had already left. It does not count as right
benchmark.method.formula.unresolved: Runs without a decision (no answer because of a technical failure) leave the denominator and are counted apart
benchmark.method.truthText: Each case's right answer was set in advance from the company records and frozen in its definition. The engine is never told it. Cases whose answer is disputed are not scored.
benchmark.method.interval: The 95% interval is the range a rate would mostly fall in if the same measurement were repeated (Wilson). The fewer the runs, the wider it is.
